fleet-maintenance-analytics.context: Daily fleet oversight combined NetSuite exports, GPS activity logs, maintenance invoices, parts inventory, and internal tracking sheets.
fleet-maintenance-analytics.problem: Disconnected sources made it difficult to see cost drivers, repeat repairs, GPS inconsistencies, asset history, and operational risk in one reliable view.
fleet-maintenance-analytics.approach: Integrated 7+ daily NetSuite extracts with GPS, maintenance, inventory, and tracking data; then applied Power Query transformations, VIN-level history, KPI dashboards, and exception detection.
fleet-maintenance-analytics.solution: A centralized analytical model and dashboard suite for maintenance cost, parts usage, downtime, GPS activity, reliability KPIs, and operational tracking.
fleet-maintenance-analytics.impact: Reduced manual report preparation by over 90%, standardized daily fleet oversight, and enabled rapid detection of operational anomalies and financial risk.

inventory-control-dashboard.context: Inventory availability, documentation, yard distribution, inspections, and deal status were tracked across NetSuite and separate operational records.
inventory-control-dashboard.problem: Conflicting spreadsheets and manual reconciliation created incorrect availability statuses, hidden documentation blocks, and inconsistent inventory visibility.
inventory-control-dashboard.approach: Unified NetSuite, yard sheets, title records, inspections, and deal pipelines; then applied status rules, automated blocks, VIN-level drill-through, aging analysis, and yard filters.
inventory-control-dashboard.solution: A centralized dashboard providing validated real-time visibility into availability, blocks, aging, documentation, and unit location.
inventory-control-dashboard.impact: Removed conflicting inventory checks, corrected dozens of availability statuses, exposed documentation and location blocks, and established clean real-time visibility for operational decisions.

warranty-claim-analytics-metro-santo-dom.context: Metro maintenance records contained spare-part failures that needed to be evaluated against technical responsibility and contract warranty criteria.
warranty-claim-analytics-metro-santo-dom.problem: Dispersed maintenance history did not provide a consistent, auditable basis for reimbursement or replacement claim decisions.
warranty-claim-analytics-metro-santo-dom.approach: Designed an Excel model that structured each failure by system, dates, description, responsibility, asset, spare part, station, and contractual criteria.
warranty-claim-analytics-metro-santo-dom.solution: A standardized failure registry, responsibility filter, eligibility matrix, and executive-ready technical claim report.
warranty-claim-analytics-metro-santo-dom.impact: Created a defensible warranty claim package with stronger traceability and a faster executive submission process for reimbursement or replacement decisions.

fare-system-transaction-fraud-detection-.summary: Investigated anomalous fare-card transaction behavior and identified three users exploiting a payment-system vulnerability that bypassed the normal recharge workflow.
fare-system-transaction-fraud-detection-.context: Fare cards were normally recharged through authorized ticket offices, machines, or approved recharge points before travel. Certain cards showed unexpected balance increases without corresponding legitimate recharge transactions.
fare-system-transaction-fraud-detection-.problem: Certain fare cards showed balance increases without corresponding legitimate recharge transactions, indicating abnormal system behavior or potential exploitation.
fare-system-transaction-fraud-detection-.approach: Correlated Card ID, timestamp, station, transaction type, balances before and after each transaction, recharge events, and fare validations to reconstruct expected versus actual card behavior and confirm repeated anomaly patterns.
fare-system-transaction-fraud-detection-.solution: Identified repeated card sequences in which balances increased without authorized recharge activity, then compared those patterns across stations and time windows.
fare-system-transaction-fraud-detection-.impact: Identified three fraudulent users exploiting a payment-system vulnerability and documented the findings for corrective security action.

fare-card-batch-integrity-investigation.summary: Identified a systematic mapping mismatch affecting approximately 125,000 MIFARE fare cards, isolated the affected inventory, supported its warranty replacement, and introduced a validation process that prevented recurrence.
fare-card-batch-integrity-investigation.context: Responsibilities within Metro Santo Domingo's Automated Fare Collection system included system maintenance, system security, technical auditing, maintenance projects, inventory and stock control, fare-card supplies, and operational incident investigation.
fare-card-batch-integrity-investigation.problem: Manufacturer-supplied identifier relationship data became misaligned with physical cards, causing backend information and administrative actions to affect incorrect cards.
fare-card-batch-integrity-investigation.approach: Analyzed card and system records, physically read sample cards, and compared those identifiers with the manufacturer-provided relationship file and the records loaded into the fare-collection backend.
fare-card-batch-integrity-investigation.solution: Identified a repeatable sequential offset after an apparent sequence error, isolated the affected inventory, and used the technical findings to support a manufacturer warranty claim.
fare-card-batch-integrity-investigation.operational_use: Introduced independent sampling across boxes and lot areas so physical card identifiers could be checked against supplied relationship data before a batch was released for operational use.
fare-card-batch-integrity-investigation.impact: Identified approximately 125,000 affected cards, supported their warranty replacement, and established an incoming-batch validation process after which the issue did not recur.

automatic-fare-equipment-reliability.summary: Analyzed recurring failures in automatic fare-card dispensers and receipt printers, identifying contamination from card and paper debris as a major reliability driver and adjusting preventive-maintenance and spare-parts strategies accordingly.
automatic-fare-equipment-reliability.context: Automatic disposable fare-card dispensers and receipt printers within Metro Santo Domingo's Automated Fare Collection system required preventive and corrective maintenance to remain available for passenger operations.
automatic-fare-equipment-reliability.problem: Dispensing rollers and printer sensors were becoming contaminated faster than expected, causing card-feed failures, printer faults, and recurring corrective maintenance.
automatic-fare-equipment-reliability.approach: Reviewed preventive and corrective maintenance behavior, traced each recurring fault from equipment operation through contamination and service failure, and compared actual field behavior with nominal component-life and maintenance expectations.
automatic-fare-equipment-reliability.solution: Adjusted dispenser and printer cleaning and inspection tasks to the contamination mechanisms observed in service, and increased dispensing-roller stock to reflect actual replacement demand.
automatic-fare-equipment-reliability.operational_use: Maintenance work could address known contamination mechanisms before they developed into recurring equipment faults, while spare-parts planning reflected field demand.
automatic-fare-equipment-reliability.impact: Adjusted preventive-maintenance practices and spare-parts planning to reflect actual operating conditions and observed component failure behavior.

turnstile-deployment-management-line-2b-.context: Metro Santo Domingo Line 2B required new station access barriers across civil, electrical, software, supplier, and station-operations workstreams.
turnstile-deployment-management-line-2b-.problem: The rollout had compressed night windows, strict station handover times, mixed barrier configurations, and cross-team dependencies while stations still needed to reopen each morning.
turnstile-deployment-management-line-2b-.approach: Coordinated station-by-station execution boards, nightly cutover plans, equipment staging, mixed-turnstile installation logic, integrated testing, and rapid issue escalation.
turnstile-deployment-management-line-2b-.solution: A synchronized deployment sequence connecting physical installation, electrification, control logic, software validation, and morning-readiness checkpoints.
turnstile-deployment-management-line-2b-.impact: Updated barriers across 10 stations in one and a half weeks through overnight replacement, minimizing service downtime and preserving consistent morning reopening readiness.

techloc-fleet-service-control.summary: Operational intelligence system connecting vehicle telemetry, geolocation, customer/account, and inventory-control data to identify and prioritize problematic assets and accounts.
techloc-fleet-service-control.context: Fleet and asset operations produced vehicle telemetry, geolocation, customer/account, and inventory-control data that needed to be interpreted together to understand asset status and financial exposure.
techloc-fleet-service-control.problem: GPS location alone did not show which accounts or assets required action. Operational review needed to connect movement state, duration, history, routes, recurring locations, current location, and asset status with customer balance and inventory information.
techloc-fleet-service-control.approach: Developed TechLoc to combine telemetry, geospatial, account, and inventory/control information in one analytical workflow structured around movement behavior, location patterns, operational status, and financial exposure.
techloc-fleet-service-control.solution: An operational intelligence system that connects asset behavior and location with customer/account and inventory conditions, allowing problematic accounts and assets to be identified, investigated, and prioritized instead of merely displayed on a map.
techloc-fleet-service-control.analytics: Analyzes parked or moving status and duration, movement history, routes, frequently visited locations, current asset location, GPS/telemetry signals, inventory and vehicle-control information, and operational asset status.
techloc-fleet-service-control.operational_use: Supports investigation and prioritization of problematic accounts and assets for collections, recovery, repossession, service, and inventory-control follow-up using combined operational and financial context.
techloc-fleet-service-control.impact: Contributed to reducing monthly outstanding customer balance from approximately $1.5M to approximately $130K and to an approximately 60% reduction in the number of vehicles placed Out for Repossession each month.

pulse-operational-workspace.context: Teams coordinating many workstreams need portfolio visibility, flexible execution views, service discovery, and guidance within the same operating environment.
pulse-operational-workspace.problem: Separate tools and rigid workflows made it harder to maintain a shared view of priorities, deadlines, workload, completion, and delivery risk.
pulse-operational-workspace.approach: Designed a responsive command layer with workspace summaries, configurable boards, table, Kanban, Gantt and calendar views, connected data, a geospatial service HUB, and role-aware guidance.
pulse-operational-workspace.solution: A focused workspace combining portfolio monitoring, board execution, service discovery, relationships, sharing controls, and in-product learning.
pulse-operational-workspace.impact: Reduced tool switching, standardized follow-up, and created a shared view of priorities and delivery risk while preserving flexibility at the board level.
